subject: 4A93A1AFA0B44305BB29CFD7BF83CFC4
introduction: When a believer wrote to ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in distress at having failed some test, he very often answered with Peter: the chief apostle denied his Lord three times in a night, and became the rock. To those ashamed of their past he offered Paul, who persecuted the church and became its greatest teacher. This guide gathers those answers, and his reading of “upon this rock” as Peter’s faith and not his person. The New Testament tells both stories without softening them, the denial and the tears, “Saul, Saul”, “the least of the apostles”, and adds what the readings pass over: “Get thee behind me, Satan”, and Paul withstanding Peter to his face.
questions: Why would the Gospels record the failure of their chief apostle? Why does ‘Abdu’l-Bahá keep returning to it?
What is the difference between Peter’s failure and Judas’s?
Paul never forgot that he had persecuted the church. How does a person carry a past like that usefully?
If the rock is Peter’s faith and not Peter, what follows?

outside.why: The reading explains this verse: thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church. The rock, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says, is Peter’s faith and confession, not his person.
No wonder thou hast fallen into tests: Peter denied three times. And Peter went out, and wept bitterly.
After the resurrection the one who denied three times was asked three times: lovest thou me? Feed my sheep.
Many were bad in the beginning and good in the end, like Paul. Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?
Paul worked against Christ, and when confirmed served. I am the least of the apostles, because I persecuted the church of God. But by the grace of God I am what I am.
One of the scorners. Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief.
Tests are inevitable. Simon, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: but I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not.
The Rock, in the moment of test, was not firm. To the same Peter, in the same chapter as the rock: get thee behind me, Satan.
The weakness even of his belief. O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?

Consider the severity of tests, that Peter denied. He was fallible afterwards too: Paul says, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed. What does the readings’ use of Peter’s failures imply about the authority later claimed in his name?
The fisherman called as the Spirit passed by. Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.
When thou hearest the call, say “Here am I”; behold Peter. Here am I; send me.
And Paul at the end: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith.

shortfall: Forty further readings repeat the two examples, Peter’s denial and Paul’s conversion, to other correspondents in nearly the same words.
